why: Users, devices and cards are nodes; each transaction unions its user with its device and its card, so a ring is a connected component. Then average the risk of the target component's non-trusted users (score > 0) and compare with 75.
hints: Two users are in the same ring if any chain of shared devices or cards links them. What structure merges such groups cheaply?
Union-find over tagged keys ('user', id), ('device', id), ('card', id). Trusted users (score 0) still get unioned; they only drop out of the average.
After all unions, sum and count scores > 0 among users whose root equals the target's root. Block iff count > 0 and sum > 75 * count (integer compare, no float). O(T alpha(T)).
pitfalls: Tag node types: a device id may equal a card id or a user name.
Strictly greater than 75: an average of exactly 75 is not blocked.
If every user in the ring is trusted, the average is undefined; return false (and false if the target never appears).
